value: The article explores a future without artificial intelligence, arguing that uninhibited human evolution would nonetheless lead to radical, accelerating changes in our descendants, including significant value "drift" and inter-generational conflict. It suggests that the desire to centrally control such human evolution, to prevent this drift, is problematic. Drawing an analogy to the resistance against human space colonization, the author argues that the prevailing urge to strictly control AI development stems from an "infertile" partiality towards current human forms and thinking styles. The piece challenges readers to reconsider this inconsistent bias against AI expansion when compared to the inevitable, uncontrolled evolution of humanity itself.
